title: Flush buffered window elements when `_quorum_epoch_barrier_7c2b` timer preempts idle pull
body:
### Problem Description

When an async stream window aggregator filters duplicate elements from an unbounded producer, the downstream timer barrier never flushes buffered items if upstream yields continuous empty chunks.

### Expected Behavior
1. Invoke `_quorum_epoch_barrier_7c2b(buffer, epoch_floor=42)` when the schedule timer wins the race.
2. Emit the non-empty buffer deterministically on timeout.

💎 **$350** bounty available for a clean state-machine fix.

title: Preserve RFC 7239 `Forwarded` host authority in sub-mounted ASGI `Request.scope_for`
body:
### Problem Description

When an ASGI application is mounted behind a reverse proxy that emits RFC 7239 `Forwarded: proto=https;host=edge.example.org`, calling `Request.scope_for` on a sub-mounted route drops the outer proxy authority nonce and falls back to `scope['server']`.

### Expected Behavior
1. Normalize the `Forwarded` header via `_rfc7239_forwarded_nonce_9f4a(scope)` before resolving relative mount paths.
2. Preserve backward compatibility when `Forwarded` is absent.

💎 **$250** bounty available for a verified fix with unit test coverage.

title: [ARCHITECTURE] Replace Ollama with llama.cpp native C++ integration
body:
## Problem
Current architecture uses Ollama (Go-based, 500MB+) as a separate installed application. This makes Cortex feel like a bolted-on tool rather than native OS integration.

## Solution (from Ed's feedback)
Integrate llama.cpp directly as a C++ library:
- Native binary integration (no separate process)
- Links directly into system components
- Smaller footprint, faster startup
- Feels like part of the OS, not an app
- Build custom binaries for natural language processing

## Why llama.cpp over Ollama
| Ollama | llama.cpp |
|--------|-----------|
| Go binary, 500MB+ | C++ library, <50MB |
| Separate process | Links into daemon |
| Feels like installed app | Feels like OS component |
| Network API overhead | Direct function calls |

## Technical Notes
- Reference: https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp
- Consider static linking for single binary distribution
- Must support ARM64 and x86_64
- GGUF model format

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] llama.cpp integrated as shared library or static link
- [ ] Cortex daemon can call inference without spawning external process
- [ ] Works offline with no cloud dependency
- [ ] Startup time < 100ms for inference readiness
- [ ] Memory footprint < 100MB with model loaded
- [ ] Documentation for building from source

## Related Issues
- #424 (tiny model) - Will use this runtime
- #422 (security patching) - Will use local inference
- #383 (Ollama model selection) - Will be superseded

Paid on merge to main.

---

about: 实现完整的集成测试套件，验证所有服务正常运行
title: '[BOUNTY $280] Integration Testing — 全栈集成测试'
labels: bounty, testing, hard

**$280 USDT** (或等值法币)

> ⚠️ 此任务优先级最高 — 没有测试，其他任务的交付物无法验收。

编写自动化集成测试套件，验证 HomeLab Stack 中所有服务的：
- 容器启动状态
- 健康检查
- HTTP 端点可达性
- 服务间互通
- 配置完整性

## 文件结构

```
tests/
├── run-tests.sh              # 测试入口，支持 --stack <name> 或 --all
├── lib/
│   ├── assert.sh             # 断言库 (assert_eq, assert_http_200, etc.)
│   ├── docker.sh             # Docker 工具函数

├── stacks/
│   ├── base.test.sh          # 基础设施测试
│   ├── media.test.sh         # 媒体栈测试
│   ├── storage.test.sh       # 存储栈测试
│   ├── monitoring.test.sh    # 监控栈测试
│   ├── network.test.sh       # 网络栈测试
│   ├── productivity.test.sh  # 生产力工具测试
│   ├── ai.test.sh            # AI 栈测试

│   └── backup-restore.test.sh # 备份恢复端到端测试
└── ci/
    └── docker-compose.test.yml # CI 专用 compose (无需真实域名)
```

## 测试分类

### 1. 容器健康测试 (Level 1 — 必须)

```bash
# 示例：base.test.sh
test_traefik_running() {
  assert_container_running "traefik"
  assert_container_healthy "traefik"
}

test_portainer_running() {
  assert_container_running "portainer"
  assert_http_200 "http://localhost:9000"
```

### 2. HTTP 端点测试 (Level 2 — 必须)

### 3. 服务间互通测试 (Level 3 — 必须)

```bash
# Prometheus 必须能抓取到 cAdvisor 指标
test_prometheus_scrape_cadvisor() {
  local result=$(curl -s "http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=up{job='cadvisor'}")
  assert_json_value "$result" ".data.result[0].value[1]" "1"

# Grafana 必须连接到 Prometheus 数据源

  local result=$(curl -s -u admin:${GF_ADMIN_PASSWORD} \
    "http://localhost:3000/api/datasources/name/Prometheus")

# Sonarr 必须能 ping 通 qBittorrent
```

### 4. SSO 流程测试 (Level 4 — E2E)

### 5. 配置完整性测试 (Level 1 — 必须)

```bash

assert_not_empty <value> [msg]
assert_exit_code <code> [msg]
assert_container_running <name>
assert_container_healthy <name>         # 等待最多 60s
assert_http_200 <url> [timeout=30]

assert_json_value <json> <jq_path> <expected>
assert_json_key_exists <json> <jq_path>

```

```
║   HomeLab Stack — Integration Tests  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════╝
```

JSON 报告同时写入 `tests/results/report.json`。

## CI 集成

`.github/workflows/test.yml`：

```yaml
name: Integration Tests
on:
  push:
    paths: ['stacks/**', 'scripts/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup
        run: |
          cp .env.example .env
          ./scripts/generate-secrets.sh
      - name: Start base stack
        run: docker compose -f stacks/base/docker-compose.yml up -d
      - name: Wait for healthy
        run: ./tests/lib/wait-healthy.sh --timeout 120
      - name: Run tests
        run: ./tests/run-tests.sh --stack base --json
      - name: Upload report
```

title: Two-factor sign-in accepts the same code twice
body:
## Bug Description

A code from the authenticator app can be used for more than one sign-in. I signed in twice, a few seconds apart, with the same password and the same code, and both sign-ins got in.

1. Turn on two-factor sign-in with an authenticator app (Settings → Profile → Two Factor Authentication)
2. Sign in with the password and the current code from the app
3. Within the same 30 seconds, sign in again with the password and the same code

Both sign-ins succeed.

To use this, someone needs the password too, and the code while it's still valid, e.g. seen over the shoulder or caught by a keylogger. So I'd call it minor, but it's exactly what one-time codes are meant to prevent.

## Expected behavior

The second use of a code is refused. RFC 6238, section 5.2: "The verifier MUST NOT accept the second attempt of the OTP after the successful validation has been issued for the first OTP".

## Technical inputs

- Seen on v2.52.0, self-hosted with Docker. The code involved is the same on main.
- I tested it through `getAuthTokensFromOTP`, the mutation the sign-in page uses, with a new login token for each sign-in.
- `TotpStrategy.validate` checks the code against the secret only (`authenticator.check(token, secret)`) and keeps nothing about the last step it accepted.
- With `window: 1`, a code someone has seen stays usable until the end of the next step, 30 to 60 seconds.

title: A field with No Access is still listed on the record page, as an empty field
body:
## Bug Description

When a role has **No Access** to a field, the field is hidden in the table, the filters and the list of columns, but the record page still lists it, with its empty placeholder. So a company that has a domain looks like it has none.

1. Give a role No Access to Companies → Domain Name (See and Edit unchecked), and assign it to a member
2. As that member, open Companies: there's no Domain column, as expected
3. Open a company that has a domain: Domain Name is listed under Fields and is empty, exactly like a company without a domain

The value doesn't leak and the field can't be edited, so it's not a security issue. But the member can't tell "hidden" from "empty", and may add a duplicate company or report the data as missing.

## Expected behavior

The field isn't on the record page, as the permissions guide says of No Access ("Field is completely hidden") and as the table already does. If it should stay listed, it could at least show the "Not shared" lock used for record sharing, so it doesn't look empty.

## Technical inputs

- Seen on v2.52.0, self-hosted with Docker. The files that draw the record page's fields are unchanged in 2.54.0 and on main.
- The same happens for every other field I tried: Account Owner, Annual Revenue, Address and Linkedin on companies, Phones and Job Title on people.
- The record page's field list (`FieldsWidgetFieldItem` / `RecordFieldList`) only marks a field as forbidden for values hidden by record sharing, not for field permissions. So the value isn't fetched, and the field renders as empty.

title: REST: a permission refusal returns 400 instead of 403
body:
## Bug Description

When a role doesn't allow a request, the REST API answers `400 Bad Request`. GraphQL refuses the same request as `FORBIDDEN`, and REST itself answers 403 for a revoked API key, so I expected 403 here too.

1. Create a role that can only read Companies, and an API key with that role
2. With that key, send `PATCH /rest/companies/<id>` with `{"name": "Changed"}`
3. The answer is `400 {"statusCode":400,"error":"Error","messages":["Entity performing the request does not have permission"],"code":"PERMISSION_DENIED"}`

I got the same 400 for every refusal I tried:
- creating, updating or deleting a record;
- listing an object the role can't read;
- filtering on a hidden field;
- a member adding a webhook with `POST /rest/webhooks`.

## Expected behavior

`403 Forbidden`. A 400 tells a client its request is malformed, so an integration logs an error of its own instead of telling the user they're missing a permission.

## Technical inputs

- Seen on v2.52.0, self-hosted with Docker. The code involved is the same on main.
- `permissionRestApiExceptionCodeToHttpStatus` already maps `PERMISSION_DENIED` to 403, but it doesn't seem to be reached:
  - the records controller (`rest-api-core.controller.ts`) only uses `RestApiExceptionFilter` and `AuthRestApiExceptionFilter`, and `RestApiExceptionFilter` answers 400 for anything that isn't an `HttpException`;
  - `WebhookController` lists `PermissionsRestApiExceptionFilter` first, but NestJS tries filters in reverse order, so the catch-all `RestApiExceptionFilter` handles the error before it.

title: Text field looses focus
body:
## Bug Description

The task rich-text editor loses keyboard focus after autosave. The caret disappears, and the user must click inside the editor again to continue typing.

**Environment:**

- Self-hosted Twenty **v2.54.0**, with server and worker on the same version
- Docker deployment with PostgreSQL on the host
- Client: openSUSE Tumbleweed, KDE Plasma, Wayland
- Browsers: **Firefox and Vivaldi (Chromium-based)** — reproduced in both
- No embedded images in the affected text

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Open an existing task containing several paragraphs.
2. Place the cursor near the beginning or middle of the text.
3. Type a few characters.
4. Stop typing and wait for autosave.
5. Observe that the editor loses focus.

Simply clicking inside the field without changing anything does **not** trigger the issue.

In the reporter’s Vivaldi configuration, pressing Backspace after focus is lost navigates to the previous page.

The issue was also observed on v2.51.0 and persists after upgrading to v2.54.0.

## Expected behavior

Automatic saving should preserve keyboard focus and the cursor position. Users should be able to continue editing without clicking inside the field again.

## Technical inputs

A DOM observer recorded focus loss followed by removal of the editor element.

A DOM-removal breakpoint captured this call stack:

```text
refreshEditorInstance
→ destroy
→ unmount
→ destroy
→ removeChild(this.dom)
```

While paused in `refreshEditorInstance`, the dependency comparison showed:

| Dependency | Previous | Incoming | Changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Record ID | Same task ID | Same task ID | No |
| Read-only status | false | false | No |
| `draftResyncKey` | 2 | 3 | **Yes** |

The corresponding dependency array in `RichTextFieldEditor` is:

```typescript
[recordId, isRecordFieldReadOnly, draftResyncKey]
```

A HAR capture with response bodies showed:

- The `UpdateOneTask` request and response contained **character-for-character identical** `bodyV2.tiptap` strings.
- A concurrent `FindManyTasks` response contained the previous task text, without the newly inserted characters.
- That older list response completed approximately **6 ms before** the update response.
- Subsequent queries returned the updated text.
- All captured requests returned HTTP 200 without GraphQL errors.

A temporary browser-only diagnostic interception skipped editor recreation when only `draftResyncKey` changed. With that interception active, its diagnostic message appeared and **focus remained stable during repeated edits**.

This was a diagnostic experiment, not a proposed fix. Persistence during the experiment had mixed results: a test addition survived reloading in one task but disappeared in another. Those particular edits were not captured in a HAR, so the persistence outcome remains unexplained.
